title: 1979 AHSME Problem 20
statement: If \(a=\frac12\) and \((a+1)(b+1)=2,\) then the radian measure of \(\operatorname{Arctan}a+\operatorname{Arctan}b\) equals

solutions.text:
Substituting \(a=\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(b=\frac{1}{3}.\) If \(u=\operatorname{Arctan}a\) and \(v=\operatorname{Arctan}b,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} \tan(u+v)&=\frac{a+b}{1-ab}\\ &=\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{6}}\\ &=1. \end{aligned} \] Both angles are positive and their sum is less than \(\frac{\pi}{2},\) so \(u+v=\frac{\pi}{4}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
